_doc: [OPUS-5] sparq-org/sparq#5799 — run-body failure-swallow waivers. A GitHub Actions step can be made unable to fail DECLARATIVELY (`continue-on-error:`) or IMPERATIVELY, inside the `run:` body, with `cmd || true` / `set +e`. The second form is invisible to YAML-structure checks: the step reports success, the job stays green, and `ci-summary / gate` counts a check-run that asserted nothing. scripts/check-workflow-run-swallow.py closes that hole for every job that GATES (i.e. every job NOT declared in .github/advisory-registry.json — the same load-bearing definition ci_summary_gate.py has used since #3773). W1 flags a statement-level `|| true` / `|| :`; commands whose non-zero exit is a DATA outcome or a diagnostic print (grep/cat/ls/find/tail/... — the checker's OBSERVATIONAL_COMMANDS set) need no entry here. Everything else — git, gh, npm, cargo, python3, any repo script — must be declared in this file with a REASON, so the next one has to be argued for rather than merely typed. Each entry needs {workflow, job_id, match, reason, registered}: `match` is a substring of the normalised logical command (>= 12 chars, so it pins the specific command rather than rubber-stamping the job), and W3 fails if it matches nothing live, so a waiver cannot rot into a standing pre-authorisation for a future swallow. THIS IS A RATCHET, NOT AN APPROVAL LIST: the 14 entries below are the complete set of W1-flagged sites on main as of 2026-09-02 (out of 22 `|| true` sites in gating jobs; the other 8 are observational and need no entry), each one read in context and found intentional. Adding an entry is a deliberate act; removing a swallow is always preferred to declaring it. Precedent that this failure mode is real and not theoretical: the PR #4211 review found `gh issue edit --add-label "$l" || true` in triage-issue.yml silently dropping ROUTING labels when a label did not exist, leaving `status:ready` set without its paired role label — the `|| true` on that call was deleted, and the comment block above the step records why.

waivers.reason: History deepening for a regression-attribution `git log baseline..HEAD` after a shallow checkout. Both fetch spellings are tried because `--unshallow` errors on a repo that is already complete; the trailing `|| true` covers the case where neither is needed. If the history is still too shallow the attribution step downstream reports that itself, so no verdict is silenced here.

Cleanup on the failure branch of `if git fetch origin main && git rebase FETCH_HEAD`. The rebase is a best-effort retry of the perf-floor commit against a main tip that moved during the long bench job; aborting a rebase that never started is not a failure. The perf gate itself is a separate, unswallowed step.

Best-effort disk reclamation between the two attempts of the sq-c76x transient-shard self-heal, in case the first attempt was a `No space left` race that left partial extraction behind. Reclaiming zero bytes is a legitimate outcome; the retried shard's own exit code is captured and re-raised (`exit "$rc"`) two lines above, so the shard verdict is unaffected.

The cone coverage REPORT step (`--mode report`), which renders the measured cone into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. Its own header states it never fails the shard: coverage-gate.py --check-robust, run unswallowed in the preceding step, is the sole coverage gate. A rendering failure must not red a shard whose coverage gate passed.

Cleanup on the `else` branch of the premerge merge probe. The non-zero merge exit is NOT swallowed — it is the signal, recorded as `merged=false` in $GITHUB_OUTPUT on the line above and branched on downstream. Aborting the merge only restores the working tree.

The anti-OOM invariant between Kani harnesses: reap any orphaned cbmc solver before the next harness starts. pkill exits 1 when there is nothing to reap, which is the expected and desired state. The harness verdict is captured separately on the line above (`&& ec=0 || ec=$?`) and acted on.

Deliberate, documented verdict RECLASSIFICATION, not a swallow. `cargo miri nextest` exits 100 both when a heavy loader test TIMED OUT (known cost debt, sq-0s15k) and when Miri found genuine UB, and the raw code cannot tell them apart — so the lane concluded `failure` every night on tracked debt and masked whether Miri found anything. The run emits a libtest-json-plus event stream to a file, and the NEXT step ('Classify shard verdict') parses it and exits 1 on a real UB/assertion failure. That classifier step is the shard verdict and carries no swallow.

Probe, not an assertion. It asks the registry whether the just-published version carries a provenance attestation; a package published WITHOUT provenance makes `npm view` exit non-zero, which is exactly the case the following lines must inspect rather than crash on under `set -euo pipefail`. The verdict is the emptiness test on $att, which fails the job unswallowed.

Same provenance-attestation probe as publish.yml:npm, for the eyereasoner-compat package. The `|| true` keeps a missing-attestation registry response from aborting under `set -euo pipefail` before the explicit emptiness check can report it.

Same provenance-attestation probe as publish.yml:npm, for the solid-server package. The `|| true` keeps a missing-attestation registry response from aborting under `set -euo pipefail` before the explicit emptiness check can report it.

Quarantine labelling for an untrusted author. Both labels are on ONE call, so this cannot half-apply the way the #4211 defect did; the quarantine's load-bearing half is that untrusted content is not acted on, which is enforced by the `if:` conditions on the downstream steps, not by this label write. Tolerated so a forge hiccup on a cosmetic label cannot red the triage lane. NB the ROUTING label write in the same job deliberately carries NO swallow (see the [OPUS-5] fail-closed comment block above it).

waivers.match: so the approval no longer applies
waivers.reason: Best-effort courtesy comment explaining a re-quarantine after a revision-bound approval lapsed. It is a notification; the re-quarantine itself is the label write, and a failed comment must not red the lane.

Best-effort courtesy comment explaining first-time quarantine to a non-collaborator. It is a notification; the quarantine itself is the label write plus the downstream `if:` conditions, and a failed comment must not red the lane.

This `|| true` is what makes the label create IDEMPOTENT: `gh label create` exits non-zero when the label already exists, which is the common case. It is the fix from the #4211 review, not the bug — the ensure-then-write ordering exists so the single all-or-nothing `gh issue edit` that follows cannot fail on a missing label. The function already refuses any name outside the closed role:/status:/needs: set.
